label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional difficulties. Despite advanced educational attainment, heavy digital engagement may coincide with or exacerbate their psychological distress.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness despite likely digital connectivity, suggesting superficial or unsatisfying online social interactions
Higher depressive symptoms including possible low mood, fatigue, and reduced motivation
Notably high anxiety symptoms — the highest of the three distress indicators — pointing to persistent worry or nervousness
Extended daily screen time exceeding 5 hours, which may reflect both occupational demands and coping or avoidance behaviors
Co-occurrence of all three distress dimensions, indicating a compounding emotional burden rather than isolated symptoms
tone: Strained and quietly overwhelmed; intellectually capable yet emotionally burdened, navigating persistent inner distress beneath a surface of high achievement and digital engagement

label: Resilient Well-Adjusted Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They score well below typical thresholds on all three psychological distress measures, suggesting a generally positive mental health status with minimal emotional distress.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77 on normalized scale), indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33), suggesting stable mood and functional well-being
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.09), reflecting very low worry or nervousness
Moderate and controlled screen/internet usage (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment (graduate degree or above)

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures individuals who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they appear to manage their emotional well-being effectively, suggesting a dissociation between perceived social isolation and clinical mood disturbance. Their moderate daily screen time (1-3 hours) and high educational attainment may reflect structured routines and cognitive resources that buffer against more severe psychological distress.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1-3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Maintains low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) despite elevated loneliness
Exhibits low anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) suggesting effective emotional regulation
Moderate daily screen use (1-3 hours) indicating balanced digital engagement
Highly educated, potentially leveraging cognitive and structural coping strategies
tone: Quietly isolated yet psychologically stable; reflective and self-sufficient rather than distressed
